import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

countries = ['Niger', 'Nigeria', 'Norway', 'Oman', 'Pakistan', 'Bangladesh', 'Kenya', 'Vietnam']
employment_metrics = ['Formal Employment', 'Informal Employment', 'Registered Businesses', 'Public Sector Employment']

employment_data = {
    'Niger': {
        'Formal Employment': [30, 32, 31, 34, 33, 35, 36, 37],
        'Informal Employment': [70, 68, 69, 66, 67, 65, 64, 63],
        'Registered Businesses': [15, 16, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23],
        'Public Sector Employment': [4, 5, 4, 5, 6, 6, 7, 5]
    },
    'Nigeria': {
        'Formal Employment': [40, 42, 41, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47],
        'Informal Employment': [60, 58, 59, 57, 56, 55, 54, 53],
        'Registered Businesses': [25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32],
        'Public Sector Employment': [6, 7, 6, 7, 8, 8, 9, 7]
    },
    'Norway': {
        'Formal Employment': [90, 91, 90, 92, 93, 92, 94, 93],
        'Informal Employment': [10, 9, 10, 8, 7, 8, 6, 7],
        'Registered Businesses': [85, 86, 87, 86, 88, 87, 89, 88],
        'Public Sector Employment': [27, 28, 27, 28, 29, 28, 29, 28]
    },
    'Oman': {
        'Formal Employment': [75, 76, 77, 78, 79, 80, 81, 80],
        'Informal Employment': [25, 24, 23, 22, 21, 20, 19, 20],
        'Registered Businesses': [65, 66, 67, 68, 69, 70, 71, 72],
        'Public Sector Employment': [23, 24, 23, 24, 25, 25, 24, 25]
    },
    'Pakistan': {
        'Formal Employment': [48, 49, 50, 51, 52, 53, 54, 55],
        'Informal Employment': [52, 51, 50, 49, 48, 47, 46, 45],
        'Registered Businesses': [35, 36, 37, 38, 39, 40, 41, 42],
        'Public Sector Employment': [12, 13, 12, 13, 14, 14, 13, 14]
    },
    'Bangladesh': {
        'Formal Employment': [47, 48, 49, 50, 51, 52, 53, 54],
        'Informal Employment': [53, 52, 51, 50, 49, 48, 47, 46],
        'Registered Businesses': [38, 39, 40, 41, 42, 43, 44, 45],
        'Public Sector Employment': [8, 9, 8, 9, 10, 10, 11, 9]
    },
    'Kenya': {
        'Formal Employment': [22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 25],
        'Informal Employment': [78, 77, 76, 75, 74, 73, 72, 75],
        'Registered Businesses': [18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 22],
        'Public Sector Employment': [7, 8, 7, 8, 9, 9, 8, 7]
    },
    'Vietnam': {
        'Formal Employment': [50, 51, 52, 53, 54, 55, 56, 55],
        'Informal Employment': [50, 49, 48, 47, 46, 45, 44, 45],
        'Registered Businesses': [42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47, 48, 49],
        'Public Sector Employment': [9, 10, 9, 10, 11, 11, 10, 9]
    }
}

data = []
for country in countries:
    for metric in employment_metrics:
        for value in employment_data[country][metric]:
            data.append({
                'Country': country,
                'Employment Metric': metric,
                'Value': value
            })

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="pastel")

violin = sns.violinplot(
    data=df[df['Employment Metric'] != 'Public Sector Employment'],
    x='Country',
    y='Value',
    hue='Employment Metric',
    legend=False,
    split=True,
    inner='quartile',
    scale='width',
    palette='Set2'
)

violin.set_title('Distribution of Employment Metrics by Country', fontsize=16, pad=20)
violin.set_xlabel('Country', fontsize=12)
violin.set_ylabel('Number of Employees', fontsize=12)
violin.legend(title='Employment Metric', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png')

---SUMMARY---
 The chart presented is a violin plot titled *Distribution of Employment Metrics by Country*, which visually compares the distribution of four key employment metrics across eight countries. The x-axis represents the countries—Niger, Nigeria, Norway, Oman, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Kenya, and Vietnam—while the y-axis denotes the percentage of the labor force, ranging from 0% to 100%. Each violin-shaped distribution corresponds to one of four employment metrics, distinguished by color: formal employment (teal), informal employment (peach), registered businesses (lavender), and public sector employment (pink).

The width of each violin reflects the density of data points at different percentage levels, with wider sections indicating higher concentrations of values. Inside each violin, horizontal lines mark the quartiles, providing insight into the spread and central tendency of the data. For instance, Norway exhibits a high concentration of formal employment, with values tightly clustered around 90% to 94%, while its informal employment distribution is narrow and concentrated near 6% to 10%. In contrast, Niger and Kenya show a broader and lower distribution for formal employment, centered around 30% to 37% and 22% to 28%, respectively, with informal employment dominating at higher percentages. Registered businesses and public sector employment metrics generally occupy lower percentage ranges, with Norway and Oman displaying the highest concentrations of registered businesses, while public sector employment remains relatively low across all countries, rarely exceeding 30%. The chart effectively highlights variations in labor market structures, illustrating stark contrasts between formal and informal employment dominance across different nations.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
print(Path('summary.txt').read_text())
table = pd.read_csv('table.csv')
print(table.head())
print(table.shape)
source = Path('chart.py').read_text()
source = source.replace("data=df[df['Employment Metric'] != 'Public Sector Employment'],", "data=df,")
source = source.replace("legend=False,", "legend=True,")
source = source.replace("set_ylabel('Number of Employees'", "set_ylabel('Percentage of Labor Force (%)'")
# Preserve width normalization using the current seaborn parameter.
source = source.replace("scale='width',", "density_norm='width',")
Path('chart.py').write_text(source)
exec(compile(source, 'chart.py', 'exec'))
ax = plt.gca()
print('Y label:', ax.get_ylabel())
print('Legend entries:', [t.get_text() for t in ax.get_legend().get_texts()])
print('Y limits:', ax.get_ylim())
print('Number of violin collections:', len(ax.collections))
